title: Does This Story Have Legs? (part 1)

image.attribution: Rayzwocker at English Wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-3.0

main_content:
Legs. They are the base of the body. And, of course, we use them to walk.

Legs have walked themselves right into many English expressions.

A useful expression using the word “legs” is to simply have them. If something has legs, it means people have interest in it.

This expression often describes a story or scandal. On the other hand, you can also say that something does not have legs, meaning no one is interested.

To have a leg up means that you are ahead of others in some competition.

For example, if you are studying rocket science in college and your mother is a rocket scientist, you have a leg up on other students.

“Having a leg up” is much better than not having a leg to stand on. This expression means that a person has no proof or evidence to support their actions.

This expression is not new. Someone used it for the time over 500 years ago!

questions.question: If, for example,​ the latest story about Julia Roberts has legs, are people uninterested in it?
options: Yes, that means it has no interest
No, that means it is of interest
It is unclear what that means
It means the story is not true
questions.answer: No, that means it is of interest

questions.question: If you have a leg up in a competition are you ahead or behind everyone else?
options: You are ahead of everyone else
You are at the same level as others
You are disqualified from the competition
questions.answer: You are ahead of everyone else

questions.question: If someone doesn’t have a leg to stand on, can he/she prove that he didn’t eat the last piece of pizza?
options: Yes, they can prove it with evidence
No, they cannot prove their innocence
Yes, they can ask others for confirmation
No, they have too many witnesses
questions.answer: No, they cannot prove their innocence
